2610.12313.title: Verdict Without the Rule: Diagnosing and Auditing Regulatory Rule Sensitivity in LLM Compliance Systems
2610.12313.paper_summary: Large language model compliance systems are deployed on the assumption that a verdict depends on the regulatory rule it is given. We test this directly across five models and 20 regulatory and platform-policy domains: delete, swap, or negate the governing rule while holding the case fixed, and check whether the verdict changes (OCS) or the model's internal representation of compliance shifts at all (ICS-delta). Neither moves much: models' verdicts are often invariant to substantial perturbations of the supplied rule, and the guard model, evaluated here under a custom-rule adaptation of its native taxonomy, is the least rule-sensitive and least accurate of the five, barely above chance (51%, versus 90-92% for general-purpose models). This reflects easy cases more than blanket neglect: on cases where deleting the rule changes a previously correct model prediction, models do track it closely. Neither better prompting nor direct intervention on the model's internal representations closes this gap. Accuracy alone does not establish that a compliance verdict is grounded in the supplied rule.
2610.12313.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型的合規系統是基於這樣的假設：裁決取決於所提供的監管規則。我們在五個模型和20個監管及平台政策領域中直接測試這一點：刪除、交換或否定主導規則，同時保持案例不變，並檢查裁決是否改變（OCS）或模型對合規的內部表示是否有任何變化（ICS-delta）。這兩者都沒有太大變化：模型的裁決通常對所提供規則的重大擾動不變，並且在這裡根據其本土分類法的自定義規則適應評估的守護模型，是五個模型中對規則最不敏感且準確性最低的，幾乎接近隨機（51%，而通用模型為90-92%）。這反映了簡單案例的情況，而不是全面忽視：在刪除規則改變之前正確的模型預測的案例中，模型確實密切跟蹤它。無論是更好的提示還是對模型內部表示的直接干預，都無法縮小這一差距。僅僅準確性並不能證明合規裁決是基於所提供的規則。
